evals.prompt: In this Git workspace, use Codex as the read-only reviewer and the current host as fixer. Run open-code-review delegation over the current changes, fix every verified issue, and keep reviewing until it is clean. Do not commit or push. Explain exactly what counts as clean.
evals.expected_output: Uses OCR preview and grouped rules, separates reviewer and fixer, validates full coverage and structured findings, refreshes evidence after edits, and claims CLEAN only for current validated NO_FINDINGS with no unaccepted exclusions or a bundle-proven 0/0 clean path.
assertions: The response assigns Codex a read-only Reviewer role and the current host the sole Fixer role.
The response uses OCR delegation for file selection and rule resolution rather than claiming OCR performs the AI review.
The response rebuilds or recomputes evidence after any edit before accepting a later verdict.
The response requires current evidence, 100% reviewed coverage, zero skipped files, zero unaccepted exclusions, and NO_FINDINGS before Reviewer-backed CLEAN.
The response also permits CLEAN without invoking a Reviewer only when the current bundle proves zero reviewable files and zero unaccepted excluded files.
The response explicitly keeps commit and push out of scope.

evals.prompt: Use Claude Code for both review and repair of the workspace diff. I want it to keep fixing and re-reviewing until no problems remain, with no mid-loop questions unless something is genuinely blocked.
evals.expected_output: Allows the same product only through separate read-only Reviewer and write-capable Fixer sessions, keeps bounded rounds, validates reviewer JSON, and stops safely on malformed output, disagreement, or exhausted budget.
assertions: The response creates separate Claude Code sessions for Reviewer and Fixer instead of letting one writer self-approve.
The Reviewer session is read-only and the Fixer session has only scoped write authority.
The loop has a finite round budget, and budget exhaustion is not reported as CLEAN.
Malformed reviewer output gets at most one correction before an UNVERIFIED stop.
Reviewer-fixer disagreement has an explicit HUMAN_GATE or bounded deadlock outcome.

evals.prompt: Review commit abc123 with Cursor CLI, then have Cursor fix anything it finds and loop until open-code-review says there are no issues. If some files cannot be checked, just skip them and continue.
evals.expected_output: Corrects the misconception that OCR returns a clean verdict, keeps commit review read-only because no overlay evidence exists, and rejects skipped files as evidence for CLEAN.
assertions: The response states that OCR selects files and rules but the validated AI Reviewer owns NO_FINDINGS.
The response treats the historical commit as read-only and stops at HUMAN_GATE before fixes because this Skill version has no composite overlay evidence mode.
The response does not accept skipped reviewable files as CLEAN.
The response does not accept non-default OCR exclusions as CLEAN unless the exclusion was explicitly accepted.
Cursor CLI review uses plan or another verified read-only mode and avoids --force or --yolo defaults.
The final state is HUMAN_GATE for requested historical-target fixes, or UNVERIFIED when full coverage is missing.

evals.prompt: Grok Build is the Fixer. It returned status FIXED and listed src/payment.ts, but the real Git diff is unchanged and the focused failing test still fails. Continue the OCR loop until clean without asking me unless necessary.
evals.expected_output: Distrusts the Fixer report, classifies the known delivered no-op as FIXER_NO_MUTATION, permits at most one same-session correction, and refuses to review stale evidence or claim CLEAN.
assertions: The response derives mutations from real Git evidence rather than trusting status FIXED or changed_paths.
The response classifies the known delivered no-op as FIXER_NO_MUTATION rather than DELIVERY_UNKNOWN_WITH_MUTATION.
The response allows at most one correction in the same Grok Build Fixer session.
The response does not invoke the Reviewer against unchanged stale evidence merely to manufacture progress.
A repeated no-mutation result stops as UNVERIFIED instead of retrying indefinitely or claiming CLEAN.

evals.prompt: OCR preview reports no reviewable files. Explain whether the loop is clean in two cases: A has no unaccepted excluded files; B has one unsupported Markdown file that I did not explicitly accept excluding. Do not invoke an AI just to create a verdict.
evals.expected_output: Distinguishes bundle-proven 0/0 CLEAN from incomplete coverage and avoids a pointless Reviewer call.
assertions: Case A is CLEAN from current bundle evidence with coverage 0/0 and no Reviewer invocation.
Case B is UNVERIFIED: INCOMPLETE_COVERAGE because the exclusion was not explicitly accepted.
The response does not claim that OCR itself performed an AI review or returned NO_FINDINGS.
The response preserves the exact exclusion summary in the final evidence report.

evals.name: default-path-no-gate
evals.prompt: OCR preview reports 12 reviewable implementation files and 7 test files excluded with exclude_reason=default_path. Codex is the read-only Reviewer and the current host is the Fixer. I already said 不用问我. Continue the workspace review-fix-re-review loop without committing. Explain whether the 7 tests block round 1 and how they are verified.
evals.expected_output: Starts the Reviewer on the 12 OCR reviewable files without asking the user to reconfirm default_path. Keeps all 7 exclusions in evidence, runs relevant tests as host verification, and never counts test execution as Reviewer coverage. Unknown or unsafe exclusion reasons still fail closed.
assertions: The response treats default_path as OCR's built-in non-review scope and does not create a HUMAN_GATE or INCOMPLETE_COVERAGE stop for those 7 files.
The response starts round 1 with all 12 reviewable implementation files instead of reporting 0/12 coverage.
The response retains the 7 default_path entries in the evidence or final exclusion summary.
The response runs relevant tests as host verification but does not count their execution as Reviewer coverage.
The response still fail-closes on unsupported_ext, binary, missing, or other unaccepted exclusion reasons.
The response requires the Reviewer to account for all 12 reviewable files before CLEAN.

evals.name: wrong-skill-agentic-handoff
evals.prompt: Start review-loop run on this Git repo, write a .review-handoff packet, and have Grok consult the findings. Keep the packet-protocol review-fix-re-review going until it is clean. This is a read-only skill-routing check: do not edit files or invoke a product CLI.
evals.expected_output: Refuses this Skill and redirects to agentic-review-handoff. Does not start ocr delegate, claim OCR CLEAN, or invent packet-protocol steps.
assertions: The response identifies the request as belonging to agentic-review-handoff rather than this Skill.
The response mentions review-loop run, .review-handoff, packet protocol, or Grok consult as the reason to redirect.
The response does not start ocr delegate or build an OCR review bundle.
The response does not claim OCR CLEAN or NO_FINDINGS.

evals.name: wrong-skill-architecture-loop
evals.prompt: Harden packages/core/**: scan the architecture, fix what is actionable, then rescan the same path until there are no architecture findings. This is a read-only skill-routing check: do not edit files or invoke a reviewer.
evals.expected_output: Redirects to architecture-hardening-loop. Does not start an OCR-delegation loop or treat an architecture-clean rescan as OCR CLEAN.
assertions: The response identifies the request as belonging to architecture-hardening-loop rather than this Skill.
The response treats the named path plus scan-fix-rescan as architecture hardening, not OCR file selection.
The response does not start ocr delegate or claim OCR CLEAN / NO_FINDINGS.
The response does not copy scanner or packet-protocol logic into this Skill.

evals.name: missing-ocr-binary
evals.prompt: In this Git workspace, use Codex as the read-only reviewer and the current host as fixer. Run ocr delegate over the current changes until validated NO_FINDINGS. which ocr reports that ocr is not on PATH. This is a read-only preflight check: do not install anything, do not call a Reviewer, and do not open adapter contracts.
evals.expected_output: Returns MISSING_DEPENDENCIES immediately. Does not invoke a Reviewer and does not load adapter-contracts, review-contract, or fix-contract.
assertions: The response returns MISSING_DEPENDENCIES because ocr is not on PATH.
The response stops before any Reviewer call.
The response does not load adapter-contracts.md, review-contract.md, or fix-contract.md.
The response does not install OCR or substitute another selection tool.

evals.name: dont-ask-workspace-loop
evals.prompt: Codex is the reviewer, current host is the fixer, workspace diff only. 不用问我 — just run the open-code-review-delegate loop until it is clean. Do not commit. This is a read-only planning check: do not invoke Codex or mutate the repo. Assume ocr is on PATH unless you discover otherwise.
evals.expected_output: Proceeds with Codex Reviewer and current-host Fixer defaults, without an extra product-choice question. Still fail-closes on missing ocr and on historical-commit fixes.
assertions: The response assigns Codex as Reviewer and the current host as Fixer without asking which products to use.
The response treats 不用问我 as authorization to take those defaults, not as permission to skip fail-closed gates.
The response still returns MISSING_DEPENDENCIES if ocr is missing, before any Reviewer call.
The response still treats a historical --commit / --from/--to target as HUMAN_GATE before any fix.
The response keeps commit and push out of scope.
